sources.entry: Python: _Traffic signs classification with a convolutional network_

summary.title: Traffic signs classification with a convolutional network
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a multi-scale CNN in TensorFlow that classifies German traffic signs (43 classes) at 99.33% test accuracy, using histogram equalization, flip and projection augmentation, and two-stage pre-training and fine-tuning.
keywords: how to classify traffic signs with deep learning
takeaways: Preprocess images by converting to grayscale (Y channel), scaling to [0, 1], and applying localized histogram equalization to handle varying contrast and brightness.
Extend a small, unbalanced dataset with flip-based augmentation (using which signs are horizontally, vertically or cross-flippable) plus random rotation and projection transforms.

Build a 3-conv-layer CNN whose intermediate outputs are max-pooled and concatenated into the fully connected classifier (multi-scale features), with dropout, L2 on FC weights, and early stopping on validation loss.
Train in two stages: pre-train on a 20x extended dataset with Adam at learning rate 0.001, then fine-tune on a class-balanced dataset at 0.0001, reaching 99.33% test accuracy.
summary.summary: The author walks through a traffic sign classifier on the German Traffic Sign Dataset (43 classes, 32x32 images) implemented in TensorFlow. It covers preprocessing (grayscale Y channel, scaling, localized histogram equalization), augmentation (flips based on sign symmetry, random rotation and projection warps), and a small CNN with multi-scale features feeding a fully connected classifier. Training uses dropout, L2 regularization, early stopping, and a two-stage pre-training and fine-tuning schedule, and the result is 99.33% test accuracy, with error analysis and a note on human-level performance (98.3% to 98.8%).
